newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ARGENTINE STILL STRUGGLING, COLOMBIA WIN AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINE STILL STRUGGLING, COLOMBIA WIN AGAIN.

text.p: Argentina continued to struggle in the World Cup qualfiers on Sunday when they were held to a 1-1 draw at home by 10-man Chile while South American group leaders Colombia won again.

Uruguay, warned by soccer's governing body FIFA to clean up their act after having seven players booked last month against Chile, received only one yellow card in their 2-0 home win over Peru but had Marcelo Otero sent off late in the game.
The violence this time came from the Chileans, who were let off lightly when they received only five bookings and a red card in Buenos Aires.
Argentina dominated their game but rarely looked like breaking through a rugged Chilean defence which was not afraid to resort to fouls -- often vicious -- to halt opposing attacks.
When Chile defender Luis Chavarria was dismissed in the 40th minute, it seemed he could be the first of several to go but his team-mates were spared further red cards by lenient refereeing.
Fernando Cornejo fired Chile ahead from a free kick early in the second half and Argentina needed a 70th minute penalty from leading scorer Gabriel Batistuta to save them from defeat.
They also had defender Roberto Ayala sent off in the 60th minute for elbowing an opponent in the face and leaving him sprawled by an advertising board.
Striker Ariel Ortega showed enormous skill for Argentina but his team-mates were not up to the same standard.
"There was something lacking," admitted coach Daniel Passarella. "We were never on top of the situation. It was not a good game for us."
The point left them third in the single South American group, from which the top four will take part in the 1998 World Cup in France.
But Argentina now face three extremly tough games -- they are away to arch-rivals Uruguay, then travel to Colombia and finally face the dreaded altitude of La Paz in Bolivia.

Argentina have already dropped two home points against Paraguay, lost to unrated Ecuador and suffered the indignity of having two goalkeepers score against them -- Paraguay's Jose Luis Chilavert and Venezuela's Rafael Dudamel -- from free kicks.
Uruguay, playing their first match under coach Julio Abuntchain, moved level on points with Argentina thanks to first half goals by Paolo Montero and Pablo Bengoechea.

Midfielder Enzo Francescoli had a penalty saved by Peru goalkeeper Julio Balerio, whose presence in the team had been the centre of a public debate because he was naturalised Peruvian after being born in Uruguay.
Colombia, without injured striker Faustino Asprilla, were still too strong for Venezuela, beating them 2-0 away and handing their hapless neighbours their sixth win in seven games.
Jorge Bermudez and Ivan Valenciano scored to increase unbeaten Colombia's lead to six points over second-placed Paraguay.

Paraguay's goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert, best known for scoring goals from penalties and free kicks, showed more orthodox skills as made a sequence of acrobatic saves to earn his team a 0-0 draw away to Bolivia.

Bolivia, who have a huge home advantage in La Paz thanks to the altitude of 3,600 metres, had also drawn their previous two home games. Paraguay had arrived three weeks before the match to acclimatise.
